fields.meta_title: Customer Effort Score Survey and Formula | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See how a customer effort score is calculated, then build a survey that asks it the moment a task ends and routes every hard answer.
fields.h1: Build a Customer Effort Score Survey That Finds the Hard Step
fields.hero_description: Describe the task you want customers to rate. Emergent builds the customer effort score question, sends it when that task ends, and keeps every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Effort Survey Has to Get Right
fields.features_subheading: Each piece below helps a low score point at the step that caused it.
fields.feature_1:
The standard statement, ready to send

Emergent writes the standard agree statement, "The company made it easy to handle my issue," on a seven-point scale. Swap in your company name and the task being rated.
fields.feature_2:
Sent the moment the task ends

Trigger the question when a return label prints or a claim is submitted. Any tool with an API can start a send, and every send is logged with the customer it went to.
fields.feature_3:
Averages and top-box shares together

Read each score two ways: the average on the seven-point scale and the share of answers at 5 or higher. Filter both by channel or by plan to see where effort climbs.
fields.feature_4:
A follow-up only for hard answers

Show "What made this hard?" only to customers whose answer is low. Their picks are counted by step, and an open box under the list catches every reason the listed steps miss.
fields.feature_5:
High-effort answers sent to an owner

Route a low score to whoever owns that article or flow, by Slack or email. The message quotes the customer's comment next to the score, and nobody needs a login to read it.
fields.feature_6:
Scores in your database, code in your repo

Every answer is a row in a database you own. Export the survey and its scoring code to your GitHub on paid plans at any point, and change either one later with a prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Tasks Worth Scoring for Effort
fields.tab_content_1:
The help article that sends readers to support

Every help article ends with the effort statement: this article made it easy to solve my problem. Scores average by article each week. Any article averaging under 5.0 goes to the docs lead in Slack, and this week "Reset two-step login" averaged 3.1 across 46 answers.
fields.tab_content_2:
Why returns feel hard, counted by step

When a shopper prints a return label, an email follows with the effort question. Anyone who answers 3 or lower picks the step that was hard from a short list. Last week, 64 of 240 answers were that low, and 38 of them named printing the label.
fields.tab_content_3:
When setup stalls, the CSM hears first

Right after an admin connects a first integration, the app asks how easy setup was. An answer of 2 or lower creates a HubSpot task for the account's customer success manager. The task names the step where the admin stalled, read from the setup log.
fields.tab_content_4:
Claim filing scored by claim type each month

Claimants who file online get a text with the effort statement as soon as the claim is submitted. Scores are reported as the share answering 5 or higher. In September, 312 of 400 claimants did, a score of 78, but water damage claims scored 59.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Customer Effort Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven decisions shape whether the score points at a fix. Emergent builds the survey around the ones you make.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask while the task is fresh
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask why only when it was hard
fields.howto_step_1_des: Score a single task, such as filing a claim or connecting an integration, instead of the whole relationship. Effort only means something when the customer can still picture each step they took. Name that task at the top of your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send the question the moment the task finishes, on the confirmation screen or in a text within the hour. A day later, customers rate their mood about your company instead of the steps. Set one trigger per task.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Use the agree statement on seven points and change only the task it names. Fixed wording lets this quarter's score sit beside last quarter's. Keep the scale in the same order every time, with strongly agree as 7.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Show the follow-up to customers who score 3 or lower, as a short list of steps with an open box under it. Customers who found the task easy never see it, and the survey stays one tap for most of them.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose one way to report it
fields.howto_step_5_des: Report either the average or the top-box share, and keep that choice. Mixing the two on one dashboard makes a steady month look like a drop. Label the method on every chart you share.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give each low score an owner
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide who hears about a hard answer: the docs lead for an article, the success manager for a stalled setup. Set thresholds so alerts stay rare enough to be read the same day. Send the rest to a weekly review.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fix the step, then measure again
fields.howto_step_7_des: Change the step customers named most often, then compare the next four weeks with the four before. If the score for that step rises while the others hold, the fix worked. Leave the question running after the change ships.

plan.angle: The top 10 (Qualtrics, IBM, Zendesk, SurveyMonkey, TechTarget, Gainsight) are glossary explainers: the definition, the 1-7 statement, a formula and a benchmark caveat. None shows a CES survey wired to the moment it scores or to what happens after a hard answer. This page answers the PAA questions plainly (how to calculate it, what is good, CSAT out of 5, the three e's) and then shows four effort surveys running inside a product: help articles averaged per page, an online return scored and broken down by the step that was hard, an integration setup whose low scores reach the account's CSM, and insurance claims reported as the share answering 5 to 7. The customer-satisfaction sibling owns ticket-close CSAT and effort; this page owns effort on self-service, returns, setup and claims.

claims_to_source: Customer effort score was introduced by Dixon, Freeman and Toman in a 2010 Harvard Business Review article
The CES statement asks customers to agree that the company made it easy to handle their issue, on a seven-point scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree
CES surveys are best sent right after the interaction, while it is fresh
CES is calculated either as the average of all answers or as the share of answers that are 5, 6 or 7
CSAT counts 4s and 5s on a 1-5 scale as satisfied and divides them by all answers
NPS asks likelihood to recommend on 0-10 and subtracts the percentage of detractors (0-6) from promoters (9-10)
Forrester's CX Index measures effectiveness, ease and emotion
